what: T1 P0.1 + P0.2 + P0.3': one content verdict per member per answer, guarded by a cheap tree stamp; discovery parallel per level; member verifications paid in parallel under a bounded worker budget

trees.w50: target/scale/w50 = 20 members x 2,503 .rs files = 50,060 files, records published per member (`verify`, pipeline only)

protocol: one fresh process per run: `target/debug/nichlink-mcp --call search --query <q> --root target/scale/<tree>`, wall clock by bash TIMEFORMAT=%R; three runs per arm; arms INTERLEAVED inside one session (arm A, arm B, arm A, arm B, ...) so load and page cache hit both arms

arms.baseline: c29ffa2 (+ docs commit 7c1eecf): `build_output_is_current` called directly by three readers; the content hash is paid twice per member (40 for 20 members)
arms.cut6_three_walks: P0.1 without the per-answer stamp memo: the stamp guard is walked by all three readers (60 walks for 20 members)
arms.cut6: P0.1: one paid entry point `freshness::verdict`, `Verified` carries a stamp (file count + newest mtime of `src/**/*.rs`, read from directory entries), `remembered()` only reuses while the stamp still matches, and `begin_answer()` shares one stamp walk per member per answer
arms.p02: P0.1 + P0.2: `parallel_map_with_workers` maps each directory level (order preserved, no nested pools)
arms.p03: P0.1 + P0.2 + P0.3': the members of a workspace are verified in parallel (`parallel_map_members`) under a bounded, machine-adaptive worker budget; the stamp walk happens inside the payment (so it runs beside the other members) and is only taken up front when there is a remembered verdict to validate; the pruning manifest is read once per member instead of twice; a verdict this answer paid for is spelled `content-verified`, not `reused`

mechanism_counts.protocol: instrumented build (eprintln in `build_output_is_current` and in `tree_stamp`), one `--call search --query child000001 --root target/scale/w50` run, counters read from stderr

baseline.note: 20 members x 2 readers, measured in the fifth cut

mechanism_counts.reading: one verdict per member, one stamp walk per member, and both now run on the worker that owes them

p03_phases.protocol: temporary eprintln timers around `search`'s phases and inside `roots_with_freshness`, one run per row, same tree and query; the rows are successive states of the same work, not three different machines

rows.state: members paid in parallel, before the other two changes
pruning manifest read once per member
stamp walk folded into the payment

p03_phases.reading: consult is what the calling thread did before the workers started (stamp walks + memo lookups); parallel_pay is the 20 content hashes plus their stamp walks on the worker pool; tree is the per-member record work (pruning manifest, one row per face). What remains is the hash itself plus a per-member manifest pass that is still sequential.

member_parallelism_probe.protocol: 8 members answered one after another, then the same 8 concurrently (`xargs -P8`), one fresh process each, wall clock
member_parallelism_probe.reading: the per-member verification is independent work and this is the evidence that parallelising it is the lever; what the tool actually uses is the bounded budget below, not -P8

worker_budget.rule: half the machine's cores, at most 8, never fewer than one core left alone; `NICH_LINK_JOBS` overrides it
worker_budget.why: the maintainer's requirement, verbatim: machine core counts differ, and a tool call must not take the user's whole machine

p02_acceptance.plan_and_records_byte_identical: measured: `verify` on a copy of target/scale/t3 (2,504 files) run with the pre-P0.2 binary and then with the P0.2 binary, both publishing into the same path; `diff -r` over the two out dirs is empty and all eight artifacts hash equal (discovery.fingerprint, file_manifest.tsv, function_manifest.tsv, generated_lib.rs, graft_plan.tsv, pruning_manifest.tsv, shape_manifest.tsv, source_scope.tsv)
p02_acceptance.older_records_stay_valid: measured: the target/scale/w50 members were published BEFORE this change; the baseline, P0.1 and P0.1+P0.2 binaries all print `freshness: content-verified` and the same `discovery.fingerprint ca0d05b9e102b8aa0300a7d40ee703d2`
p02_acceptance.pin: build_time::source_walk::discovery_tests::the_discovered_tree_does_not_depend_on_the_worker_count (200-face wide fixture where the wide level is not the root; workers 1/2/3/8/64 must agree on the tree AND on the order of the findings)

answer_wording_fixed.what: P0.1 alone silently changed what the answer says for the same work
answer_wording_fixed.now: freshness: content-verified at 23:42:15 (measured) — a verdict this answer paid for is not a reuse; only a later answer's reuse is spelled `reused`

estimation_rule: every number above is MEASURED. Where a figure in the checklist's P0 table is an estimate it is labelled as one.
open: T1 acceptance p95 <= 1 s is NOT met: 3.16-3.26 s at 50,000 files with this bounded budget (8 workers of 20 cores)

what remains: the twenty whole-tree content hashes (~1.4-1.7 s on the worker pool, which is why the budget bounds the gain: 20 members / 8 workers), one still-sequential per-member manifest pass (~0.9 s), and process startup + workspace scope (~0.5 s)

the route to <= 1 s is a budget decision (raise NICH_LINK_JOBS / the rule), not a semantic change: P0.3 (verify only the rows an answer names) is still open and would cost the negative answers their whole-tree guarantee
